+"""Standalone copy of Click's Windows console stream lookup.
+
+Vendored from ``click._winconsole._get_windows_console_stream`` so that it
+can be imported by file path without importing Click. The original module
+is based on the work by Adam Bartoš in the discussion of issue1602 in the
+Python bug tracker.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import collections.abc as cabc
+import io
+import sys
+import time
+import typing as t
+from ctypes import Array
+from ctypes import byref
+from ctypes import c_char
+from ctypes import c_char_p
+from ctypes import c_int
+from ctypes import c_ssize_t
+from ctypes import c_ulong
+from ctypes import c_void_p
+from ctypes import POINTER
+from ctypes import py_object
+from ctypes import Structure
+from ctypes.wintypes import DWORD
+from ctypes.wintypes import HANDLE
+from ctypes.wintypes import LPCWSTR
+from ctypes.wintypes import LPWSTR
+
+__all__ = ["vendored_console_stream", "vendored_console_stream_variant"]
+
+# The original module asserts ``sys.platform == "win32"`` at import time.
+# Here the native bindings are only set up on Windows, and buffer access is
+# disabled elsewhere so the lookup returns ``None`` instead of failing.
+if sys.platform == "win32":
+    import msvcrt
+    from ctypes import windll
+    from ctypes import WINFUNCTYPE
+
+    c_ssize_p = POINTER(c_ssize_t)
+
+    kernel32 = windll.kernel32
+    GetStdHandle = kernel32.GetStdHandle
+    ReadConsoleW = kernel32.ReadConsoleW
+    WriteConsoleW = kernel32.WriteConsoleW
+    GetConsoleMode = kernel32.GetConsoleMode
+    GetLastError = kernel32.GetLastError
+    GetCommandLineW = WINFUNCTYPE(LPWSTR)(("GetCommandLineW", windll.kernel32))
+    CommandLineToArgvW = WINFUNCTYPE(POINTER(LPWSTR), LPCWSTR, POINTER(c_int))(
+        ("CommandLineToArgvW", windll.shell32)
+    )
+    LocalFree = WINFUNCTYPE(c_void_p, c_void_p)(("LocalFree", windll.kernel32))
+
+    STDIN_HANDLE = GetStdHandle(-10)
+    STDOUT_HANDLE = GetStdHandle(-11)
+    STDERR_HANDLE = GetStdHandle(-12)
+
+PyBUF_SIMPLE = 0
+PyBUF_WRITABLE = 1
+
+ERROR_SUCCESS = 0
+ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY = 8
+ERROR_OPERATION_ABORTED = 995
+
+STDIN_FILENO = 0
+STDOUT_FILENO = 1
+STDERR_FILENO = 2
+
+EOF = b"\x1a"
+MAX_BYTES_WRITTEN = 32767
+
+if t.TYPE_CHECKING:
+    try:
+        # Using `typing_extensions.Buffer` instead of `collections.abc`
+        # on Windows for some reason does not have `Sized` implemented.
+        from collections.abc import Buffer  # type: ignore
+    except ImportError:
+        from typing_extensions import Buffer
+
+if sys.platform != "win32":
+    get_buffer = None
+else:
+    try:
+        from ctypes import pythonapi
+    except ImportError:
+        # On PyPy we cannot get buffers so our ability to operate here is
+        # severely limited.
+        get_buffer = None
+    else:
+
+        class Py_buffer(Structure):
+            _fields_ = [  # noqa: RUF012
+                ("buf", c_void_p),
+                ("obj", py_object),
+                ("len", c_ssize_t),
+                ("itemsize", c_ssize_t),
+                ("readonly", c_int),
+                ("ndim", c_int),
+                ("format", c_char_p),
+                ("shape", c_ssize_p),
+                ("strides", c_ssize_p),
+                ("suboffsets", c_ssize_p),
+                ("internal", c_void_p),
+            ]
+
+        PyObject_GetBuffer = pythonapi.PyObject_GetBuffer
+        PyBuffer_Release = pythonapi.PyBuffer_Release
+
+        def get_buffer(obj: Buffer, writable: bool = False) -> Array[c_char]:
+            buf = Py_buffer()
+            flags: int = PyBUF_WRITABLE if writable else PyBUF_SIMPLE
+            PyObject_GetBuffer(py_object(obj), byref(buf), flags)
+
+            try:
+                buffer_type = c_char * buf.len
+                out: Array[c_char] = buffer_type.from_address(buf.buf)
+                return out
+            finally:
+                PyBuffer_Release(byref(buf))
+
+
+class _NonClosingTextIOWrapper(io.TextIOWrapper):
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        stream: t.BinaryIO,
+        encoding: str | None,
+        errors: str | None,
+        force_readable: bool = False,
+        force_writable: bool = False,
+        **extra: t.Any,
+    ) -> None:
+        self._stream = stream = t.cast(
+            t.BinaryIO, _FixupStream(stream, force_readable, force_writable)
+        )
+        super().__init__(stream, encoding, errors, **extra)
+
+    def __del__(self) -> None:
+        try:
+            self.detach()
+        except Exception:
+            pass
+
+    def isatty(self) -> bool:
+        # https://bitbucket.org/pypy/pypy/issue/1803
+        return self._stream.isatty()
+
+
+class _FixupStream:
+    """The new io interface needs more from streams than streams
+    traditionally implement.  As such, this fix-up code is necessary in
+    some circumstances.
+
+    The forcing of readable and writable flags are there because some tools
+    put badly patched objects on sys (one such offender are certain version
+    of jupyter notebook).
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        stream: t.BinaryIO,
+        force_readable: bool = False,
+        force_writable: bool = False,
+    ):
+        self._stream = stream
+        self._force_readable = force_readable
+        self._force_writable = force_writable
+
+    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> t.Any:
+        return getattr(self._stream, name)
+
+    def read1(self, size: int) -> bytes:
+        f = getattr(self._stream, "read1", None)
+
+        if f is not None:
+            return t.cast(bytes, f(size))
+
+        return self._stream.read(size)
+
+    def readable(self) -> bool:
+        if self._force_readable:
+            return True
+        x = getattr(self._stream, "readable", None)
+        if x is not None:
+            return t.cast(bool, x())
+        try:
+            self._stream.read(0)
+        except Exception:
+            return False
+        return True
+
+    def writable(self) -> bool:
+        if self._force_writable:
+            return True
+        x = getattr(self._stream, "writable", None)
+        if x is not None:
+            return t.cast(bool, x())
+        try:
+            self._stream.write(b"")
+        except Exception:
+            try:
+                self._stream.write(b"")
+            except Exception:
+                return False
+        return True
+
+    def seekable(self) -> bool:
+        x = getattr(self._stream, "seekable", None)
+        if x is not None:
+            return t.cast(bool, x())
+        try:
+            self._stream.seek(self._stream.tell())
+        except Exception:
+            return False
+        return True
+
+
+class _WindowsConsoleRawIOBase(io.RawIOBase):
+    def __init__(self, handle: int | None) -> None:
+        self.handle = handle
+
+    def isatty(self) -> t.Literal[True]:
+        super().isatty()
+        return True
+
+
+class _WindowsConsoleReader(_WindowsConsoleRawIOBase):
+    def readable(self) -> t.Literal[True]:
+        return True
+
+    def readinto(self, b: Buffer) -> int:
+        bytes_to_be_read = len(b)
+        if not bytes_to_be_read:
+            return 0
+        elif bytes_to_be_read % 2:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "cannot read odd number of bytes from UTF-16-LE encoded console"
+            )
+
+        buffer = get_buffer(b, writable=True)
+        code_units_to_be_read = bytes_to_be_read // 2
+        code_units_read = c_ulong()
+
+        rv = ReadConsoleW(
+            HANDLE(self.handle),
+            buffer,
+            code_units_to_be_read,
+            byref(code_units_read),
+            None,
+        )
+        if GetLastError() == ERROR_OPERATION_ABORTED:
+            # wait for KeyboardInterrupt
+            time.sleep(0.1)
+        if not rv:
+            raise OSError(f"Windows error: {GetLastError()}")
+
+        if buffer[0] == EOF:
+            return 0
+        return 2 * code_units_read.value
+
+
+class _WindowsConsoleWriter(_WindowsConsoleRawIOBase):
+    def writable(self) -> t.Literal[True]:
+        return True
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _get_error_message(errno: int) -> str:
+        if errno == ERROR_SUCCESS:
+            return "ERROR_SUCCESS"
+        elif errno == ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY:
+            return "ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY"
+        return f"Windows error {errno}"
+
+    def write(self, b: Buffer) -> int:
+        bytes_to_be_written = len(b)
+        buf = get_buffer(b)
+        code_units_to_be_written = min(bytes_to_be_written, MAX_BYTES_WRITTEN) // 2
+        code_units_written = c_ulong()
+
+        WriteConsoleW(
+            HANDLE(self.handle),
+            buf,
+            code_units_to_be_written,
+            byref(code_units_written),
+            None,
+        )
+        bytes_written = 2 * code_units_written.value
+
+        if bytes_written == 0 and bytes_to_be_written > 0:
+            raise OSError(self._get_error_message(GetLastError()))
+        return bytes_written
+
+
+class ConsoleStream:
+    def __init__(self, text_stream: t.TextIO, byte_stream: t.BinaryIO) -> None:
+        self._text_stream = text_stream
+        self.buffer = byte_stream
+
+    @property
+    def name(self) -> str:
+        return self.buffer.name
+
+    def write(self, x: t.AnyStr) -> int:
+        if isinstance(x, str):
+            return self._text_stream.write(x)
+        try:
+            self.flush()
+        except Exception:
+            pass
+        return self.buffer.write(x)
+
+    def writelines(self, lines: cabc.Iterable[t.AnyStr]) -> None:
+        for line in lines:
+            self.write(line)
+
+    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> t.Any:
+        return getattr(self._text_stream, name)
+
+    def isatty(self) -> bool:
+        return self.buffer.isatty()
+
+    def __repr__(self) -> str:
+        return f"<ConsoleStream name={self.name!r} encoding={self.encoding!r}>"
+
+
+def _get_text_stdin(buffer_stream: t.BinaryIO) -> t.TextIO:
+    text_stream = _NonClosingTextIOWrapper(
+        io.BufferedReader(_WindowsConsoleReader(STDIN_HANDLE)),
+        "utf-16-le",
+        "strict",
+        line_buffering=True,
+    )
+    return t.cast(t.TextIO, ConsoleStream(text_stream, buffer_stream))
+
+
+def _get_text_stdout(buffer_stream: t.BinaryIO) -> t.TextIO:
+    text_stream = _NonClosingTextIOWrapper(
+        io.BufferedWriter(_WindowsConsoleWriter(STDOUT_HANDLE)),
+        "utf-16-le",
+        "strict",
+        line_buffering=True,
+    )
+    return t.cast(t.TextIO, ConsoleStream(text_stream, buffer_stream))
+
+
+def _get_text_stderr(buffer_stream: t.BinaryIO) -> t.TextIO:
+    text_stream = _NonClosingTextIOWrapper(
+        io.BufferedWriter(_WindowsConsoleWriter(STDERR_HANDLE)),
+        "utf-16-le",
+        "strict",
+        line_buffering=True,
+    )
+    return t.cast(t.TextIO, ConsoleStream(text_stream, buffer_stream))
+
+
+_stream_factories: cabc.Mapping[int, t.Callable[[t.BinaryIO], t.TextIO]] = {
+    0: _get_text_stdin,
+    1: _get_text_stdout,
+    2: _get_text_stderr,
+}
+
+
+def _is_console(f: t.TextIO) -> bool:
+    if not hasattr(f, "fileno"):
+        return False
+
+    try:
+        fileno = f.fileno()
+    except (OSError, io.UnsupportedOperation):
+        return False
+
+    handle = msvcrt.get_osfhandle(fileno)
+    return bool(GetConsoleMode(handle, byref(DWORD())))
+
+
+def vendored_console_stream(
+    f: t.TextIO, encoding: str | None, errors: str | None
+) -> t.TextIO | None:
+    if (
+        get_buffer is None
+        or encoding not in {"utf-16-le", None}
+        or errors not in {"strict", None}
+        or not _is_console(f)
+    ):
+        return None
+
+    func = _stream_factories.get(f.fileno())
+    if func is None:
+        return None
+
+    b = getattr(f, "buffer", None)
+
+    if b is None:
+        return None
+
+    return func(b)
+
+
+def vendored_console_stream_variant(
+    f: t.TextIO, encoding: str | None, errors: str | None
+) -> t.TextIO | None:
+    """Like :func:`vendored_console_stream`, but matches the encoding name
+    case-insensitively, so ``"UTF-16-LE"`` is accepted like ``"utf-16-le"``.
+    """
+    if encoding is not None:
+        encoding = encoding.lower()
+
+    return vendored_console_stream(f, encoding, errors)

@@ -0,0 +1,166 @@
+import importlib.util
+import io
+import pathlib
+import sys
+from unittest import mock
+
+import pytest
+
+MODULE_PATH = (
+    pathlib.Path(__file__).parent.parent / "src" / "standalone_wave6_console_stream.py"
+)
+
+
+@pytest.fixture()
+def mod():
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
+        "standalone_wave6_console_stream", MODULE_PATH
+    )
+    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+    return module
+
+
+class FakeConsole:
+    def __init__(self, fileno=1, buffer=None):
+        self._fileno = fileno
+        self.buffer = io.BytesIO() if buffer is None else buffer
+
+    def fileno(self):
+        return self._fileno
+
+
+@pytest.fixture()
+def console(mod, monkeypatch):
+    """Pretend buffers are available and every stream is a console."""
+    factory = mock.Mock(return_value="console-stream")
+    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "get_buffer", mock.Mock())
+    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "_is_console", mock.Mock(return_value=True))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "_stream_factories", {0: factory, 1: factory, 2: factory})
+    return factory
+
+
+def test_import_does_not_load_click(mod):
+    assert mod.__all__ == ["vendored_console_stream", "vendored_console_stream_variant"]
+    assert not hasattr(mod, "click")
+    assert mod._NonClosingTextIOWrapper.__module__ == mod.__name__
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform == "win32", reason="non-Windows behavior")
+def test_buffer_disabled_off_windows(mod):
+    assert mod.get_buffer is None
+    assert mod.vendored_console_stream(FakeConsole(), None, None) is None
+    assert mod.vendored_console_stream_variant(FakeConsole(), "UTF-16-LE", None) is None
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("encoding", [None, "utf-16-le"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("errors", [None, "strict"])
+def test_vendored_returns_factory_stream(mod, console, encoding, errors):
+    f = FakeConsole(fileno=1)
+    assert mod.vendored_console_stream(f, encoding, errors) == "console-stream"
+    console.assert_called_once_with(f.buffer)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("encoding", ["UTF-16-LE", "utf-8", ""])
+def test_vendored_rejects_other_encodings(mod, console, encoding):
+    assert mod.vendored_console_stream(FakeConsole(), encoding, None) is None
+    console.assert_not_called()
+
+
+def test_vendored_rejects_non_strict_errors(mod, console):
+    assert mod.vendored_console_stream(FakeConsole(), None, "replace") is None
+    assert mod.vendored_console_stream(FakeConsole(), None, "") is None
+    console.assert_not_called()
+
+
+def test_vendored_requires_console(mod, console, monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "_is_console", mock.Mock(return_value=False))
+    assert mod.vendored_console_stream(FakeConsole(), None, None) is None
+    console.assert_not_called()
+
+
+def test_vendored_unknown_fileno(mod, console):
+    assert mod.vendored_console_stream(FakeConsole(fileno=7), None, None) is None
+    console.assert_not_called()
+
+
+def test_vendored_missing_buffer(mod, console):
+    f = FakeConsole()
+    f.buffer = None
+    assert mod.vendored_console_stream(f, None, None) is None
+    console.assert_not_called()
+
+
+def test_vendored_disabled_buffer(mod, console, monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "get_buffer", None)
+    assert mod.vendored_console_stream(FakeConsole(), None, None) is None
+    console.assert_not_called()
+
+
+def test_vendored_propagates_factory_error(mod, console):
+    console.side_effect = OSError("Windows error: 6")
+    with pytest.raises(OSError, match="Windows error"):
+        mod.vendored_console_stream(FakeConsole(), None, None)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("encoding", ["UTF-16-LE", "Utf-16-Le", "utf-16-le", None])
+def test_variant_lowercases_encoding(mod, console, encoding):
+    f = FakeConsole(fileno=2)
+    assert mod.vendored_console_stream_variant(f, encoding, "strict") == (
+        "console-stream"
+    )
+    console.assert_called_once_with(f.buffer)
+
+
+def test_variant_forwards_lowercased(mod, monkeypatch):
+    inner = mock.Mock(return_value=None)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "vendored_console_stream", inner)
+    f = FakeConsole()
+    assert mod.vendored_console_stream_variant(f, "UTF-16-LE", None) is None
+    inner.assert_called_once_with(f, "utf-16-le", None)
+    inner.reset_mock()
+    mod.vendored_console_stream_variant(f, None, "strict")
+    inner.assert_called_once_with(f, None, "strict")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("encoding", ["", "UTF-8"])
+def test_variant_rejects_other_encodings(mod, console, encoding):
+    assert mod.vendored_console_stream_variant(FakeConsole(), encoding, None) is None
+    console.assert_not_called()
+
+
+def test_variant_invalid_encoding_type(mod, console):
+    with pytest.raises(AttributeError):
+        mod.vendored_console_stream_variant(FakeConsole(), 16, None)
+
+
+def test_is_console(mod, monkeypatch):
+    msvcrt = mock.Mock()
+    msvcrt.get_osfhandle.return_value = 42
+    get_mode = mock.Mock(return_value=1)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "msvcrt", msvcrt, raising=False)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "GetConsoleMode", get_mode, raising=False)
+    assert mod._is_console(FakeConsole(fileno=1)) is True
+    msvcrt.get_osfhandle.assert_called_once_with(1)
+    get_mode.return_value = 0
+    assert mod._is_console(FakeConsole()) is False
+    assert mod._is_console(object()) is False
+
+    class Unsupported:
+        def fileno(self):
+            raise io.UnsupportedOperation
+
+    assert mod._is_console(Unsupported()) is False
+
+
+def test_text_stdout_factory(mod, monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "STDOUT_HANDLE", 11, raising=False)
+    raw = io.BytesIO()
+    raw.name = "<stdout>"
+    stream = mod._stream_factories[1](raw)
+    assert isinstance(stream, mod.ConsoleStream)
+    assert stream.buffer is raw
+    assert stream.encoding == "utf-16-le"
+    assert stream.name == "<stdout>"
+    assert stream.write(b"bytes") == 5
+    assert raw.getvalue() == b"bytes"
notes:
Copied the Windows console stream code (bindings, get_buffer, stream classes, factories, _is_console, _NonClosingTextIOWrapper/_FixupStream) into a standalone module, with the native bindings behind a win32 guard and get_buffer=None on other platforms. The target body is unchanged and renamed vendored_console_stream; vendored_console_stream_variant lowercases the encoding before forwarding it. Tests load the module by file path and mock the platform APIs and factories.
